title: Beads binary resolution: skip non-executable bd candidates on Unix
outcome: Review round 27 (Claude Low). validate_beads_binary checks absolute path, regular file, shim extension and shebang, but on Unix never the execute bit; resolve_beads_binary_on_path returns the first bd that passes, so a non-executable file named bd earlier on PATH hides a valid bd later on PATH (a shell lookup would skip it), and the source reports a launch failure instead of reading. Follow-up: on cfg(unix) require metadata.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0 in validate_beads_binary (so the PATH search continues to the next candidate and a configured non-executable path is refused), with a cfg(unix) test. Not written on the Windows host: cfg(unix) code cannot be compiled or run here, and unverified code is not evidence. Pair with the Unix symlink-resolution test gap in the sibling task.
